subject.title: Feature: Add /models test-fallback command to verify fallback chain

question: Should proactive fallback validation be a distinct ordered fallback-chain command, or should https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/63145 expand `models status --probe` to cover that behavior as its canonical diagnostic mode?
rationale: Both requests exercise configured models, but one needs failover ordering and primary omission while the other is broader per-model health checking; choosing independently would create overlapping CLI semantics and duplicated provider probing.

options.title: Unify under model status
options.body: Extend `models status --probe` with an explicit ordered-fallback mode, keeping one diagnostic owner while preserving a separate all-configured-model health mode.

options.title: Keep a dedicated fallback command
options.body: Add a distinct fallback-chain command only if maintainers want slash-command access and failure-order semantics that status output cannot express cleanly.

options.title: Defer until the health probe lands
options.body: Land and evaluate the all-model health probe first, then decide whether an ordered fallback diagnostic still exposes a meaningful remaining gap.

recommendation.title: Unify under model status
recommendation.body: Extend `models status --probe` with an explicit ordered-fallback mode, keeping one diagnostic owner while preserving a separate all-configured-model health mode.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue discussion contains a detailed review of the exact CLI, slash-command, and fallback-runtime boundary, making this the strongest available product-routing signal.
